bullets.title: S&P at all-time highs, record call volumes signal blow-off risk
bullets.body: SPX hit ~7,748 (+0.2%) and touched all-time highs (~7,736) driven by US-Iran Hormuz deal hopes and AI earnings leadership. Record 4M+ S&P call options were purchased yesterday (highest ever) while SPX put-call skew reached bullish extremes per Goldman Sachs, with net L/S leverage jumping 47% to 56% in four days—the largest 4-day increase on record. Some technicians flag overbought conditions as VIX rose alongside equity strength.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz standoff: Trump signals deal in 48 hrs, Iran denies; oil +1.1%
bullets.body: Trump said a 60-day Hormuz shipping agreement with Iran and Oman could come within 48 hours, but Iranian state media flatly contradicted this, stating reopening depends on a change in US behavior. Separately, Houthis attacked and sank a vessel in the Red Sea and threatened Saudi oil tankers near Yanbu. Brent rose 1.1% to ~$80/bbl on the mixed signals; Iran also attributed cyberattacks on US water facilities in seven states to Iranian actors.

bullets.title: July ISM Services 54.1: demand/activity strong, but prices paid rebounded
bullets.body: July ISM Services PMI edged up 0.1pt to 54.1% (consensus +0.5pt), with business activity and new orders accelerating above 1H26 averages. Prices paid retraced most of the June decline, signaling sticky PCE supercore services inflation. Employment and supplier deliveries softened; company commentary flagged cost pressures and uncertainty around the Iran conflict and oil prices.

bullets.title: ADP +44K vs 70K consensus; labor market softening ahead of Friday payrolls
bullets.body: July ADP private payrolls rose only 44K, well below the 70K consensus, as JOLTS vacancies also fell. The data keeps Friday's nonfarm payroll report in sharp focus; 22V Research notes a consensus print (~4.2% unemployment, +80K headline) would keep 10-year yields stable near 4.62%, while a sub-4.2% unemployment surprise would be hawkish. One options trader is positioning for 10-year yields to rise 25bps to 4.85% by mid-August.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle intact: SpaceX targets 8-10GW NVDA compute by YE27, AVGO TPU financing could hit $300B+
bullets.body: SpaceX management targets 5-10GW of compute capacity (using NVIDIA exclusively) by end-CY27, implying ~$300B+ capex at $35B/GW—more than sufficient to underpin consensus NVDA CY27 growth targets. Goldman Sachs raised SPCX FY27 revenue forecast ~55% to $107B and expects $100B ARR run-rate by December. Separately, Blackstone held preliminary discussions on a second Google TPU-financing tranche for Anthropic potentially $35B+, and AVGO's AI XPV platform could see theoretical max exposure exceeding $300B across two labs by decade-end.

bullets.title: Texas data center audit is a quasi-moratorium; accelerates behind-the-meter plays, pressures IPPs
bullets.body: Texas Governor Abbott ordered a 40-60 day PUCT/ERCOT audit on data center interconnections, effectively halting new grid-connected development. Amazon simultaneously withdrew its Calvert, Maryland data center plans (no deal had been signed with CEG). Morgan Stanley and other analysts flag NRG and VST as most exposed IPPs, while BE, SEI, and equipment manufacturers are seen as beneficiaries of accelerated behind-the-meter adoption in 2H26.

bullets.title: Broad earnings season: EPS growth +52% YoY driving market broadening; equal-weight RSP at all-time highs
bullets.body: Russell 2000 equal-weight EPS growth is running +52% YoY, cited as a primary driver of the broadening rally with RSP hitting all-time highs. 544 Russell 2000 companies (44% of market cap) reported 2Q26 with aggregate EPS leading expectations by 9.7%. The Russell 2000 outperformed the S&P 500 by 0.1% on 8/4, up 22.4% YTD vs S&P +10.1%.

bullets.title: Macro backdrop unusually calm: yields flat, currencies stable, oil rangebound
bullets.body: Multiple sources noted that major bond yields were essentially unchanged overnight, key currencies were flat, and oil traded in a tight range, with the 10-year holding near 4.62%. The one exception was mortgage demand, which fell 2.9% in the week ended July 31 as the 30-year rate hit a one-year high of 6.81%.

bullets.title: SHOP surges 34%+ on Q2 beat; highest revenue growth since early 2022
bullets.body: Shopify Q2 revenue +33.7% YoY to $3.58B (beat by ~5pts), GMV +31.6% to $115.6B, FCF margin 18.3%—all cycle highs. Q3 guidance of low-30s revenue growth and mid-high 20s gross profit growth far exceeded consensus (+27%). JPMorgan added SHOP to its Analyst Focus List as Top Pick; shares were +22-34% pre-market.

bullets.title: ANET crushes Q2, raises FY26 guide to +40%; all 32 analysts rate Buy
bullets.body: Arista Q2 revenue $3.04B beat consensus by 7.4%; FY26 revenue growth raised to 40% from 28% with AI revenue guided ≥$3.5B. Q3 guided ~$3.3B (+11.9% above consensus). Supply chain constraints are easing with multi-year vendor agreements extending visibility into 2027; two potential new 10% customers identified. Average sell-side PT raised 20.7% to $232.50.

bullets.title: AMD -8% despite strong DC beat; GPU upside capped pre-Helios; 2027 framing bullish
bullets.body: AMD Q2 revenue $11.5B beat consensus; DC revenue $6.7B (+107% YoY). Management framed CY27 as >100% DC growth and >70% server CPU growth, with $20-25 EPS bull case. However, Q3 gross margin guidance of ~56% was below buy-side expectations and Helios GPU launch is Q4, capping near-term GPU upside. Wells Fargo and others raised PT to $700, but stock fell ~8% as the market had discounted a higher bar.

bullets.title: AI margin tailwind emerging: 150bps aggregate S&P margin improvement quantified across 25 companies
bullets.body: 22V Research quantified ~150bps aggregate operating margin improvement from AI adoption across 25 reporting companies, which if extrapolated to the S&P 500 implies minimum +10% upside to fair value (~740 index points). The firm targets S&P 8,500 on stable 10-year yields near 4.5%, with non-AI cyclicals (retailers, regional banks, transports) now becoming attractive.

bullets.title: Hormuz/ME conflict is a persistent macro headwind: GPN, BKNG cut guidance
bullets.body: Global Payments cut FY26 revenue growth guidance to 4-5% from 5% and EPS growth to 11-13% from 13-15%, explicitly attributing the reduction to the ongoing Middle East conflict's impact on its travel payments portfolio. Booking Holdings also lowered FY bookings and EBITDA growth guidance (to high-single-digits), though Q2 room night growth of +5% beat the Street's +3.7% estimate and analysts view Q3 guidance as conservative.

bullets.title: SpaceX/Starlink mobile push hits US telco stocks; CCI -9% on mobile market entry plan
bullets.body: SpaceX disclosed plans to target the US mobile market directly, pressuring AT&T and Verizon (each -1.8-1.9%) and crushing Crown Castle (CCI -9%) on fears of tower demand disruption. NVDA leads Mag-7 higher on the SpaceX exclusive AI infrastructure partnership, while TSLA underperformed as SpaceX debuted as a standalone public entity.

bullets.title: US lodging data strong: RevPAR +7.3% YoY; luxury +12.9%; urban +13%
bullets.body: US RevPAR for the week ending 8/1/26 rose 7.3% YoY to $120 (ADR +4.5%, occupancy +2.6%). Luxury led at +12.9% and urban markets surged +13% vs resort +4%. July YTD RevPAR tracking +8.4%. For 3Q26, HST and PK are tracking +9.4-9.5% vs consensus of only +3.5%, suggesting significant upside for hotel REITs relative to expectations.

bullets.title: Foxconn July sales +54% YoY to NT$946.5B—first month ever above NT$900B on AI pull-ins
bullets.body: Foxconn reported record July revenues of NT$946.5B, up 54.2% YoY and 15.2% MoM, driven by strong demand and pull-in orders for AI-related products. This is a positive read-through for AI server supply chain and NVDA/AVGO ecosystem demand durability.

bullets.title: Potential China optical transceiver ban could open $10B opportunity for US suppliers
bullets.body: JPMorgan flagged that a proposed US ban on Chinese optical transceivers could open a $10B addressable opportunity for domestic suppliers, with COHR, LITE, FN, and CRDO best positioned. Samsung's 4nm foundry capacity is also fully booked as AI/server orders surge, with 5nm being pushed as an alternative.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples re-rating: All-SaaS +5.6% weekly multiple expansion; IGV still -10.5% YTD
bullets.body: Wolfe Research noted All-SaaS trading at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales with +5.6% week-over-week multiple expansion and All-Vertical at +8.4% WoW. Despite the re-rating, IGV remains -10.5% YTD vs S&P +10.1%. AI-native cohorts continue to outpace legacy SaaS meaningfully.

bullets.title: Higher rate volatility seen as the new norm under potential Warsh Fed era
bullets.body: Multiple sources flagged that a Kevin Warsh-led Fed would likely usher in structurally higher rate volatility. BofA separately revised its year-end USD/JPY forecast to 149 from 152 following Japanese intervention, with Treasury Secretary Bessent endorsing BOJ Governor Ueda's approach to yen stability.

bullets.title: India momentum factor recovering; small/mid-caps outperforming Nifty YTD
bullets.body: JPMorgan recommends staying long India momentum as the Composite Momentum Index recovered from a 3.8% peak-to-trough correction in June-July. Small caps (+9.9% YTD) and mid-caps (+4.6% YTD) are outperforming the Nifty 50 (-5.8% YTD), with MSCI India EPS growth forecast at 11%/13% for CY26/27. Analysts characterize the July momentum correction as an air pocket, not a trend failure.
